items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1962-09-19
items.q: when I went there in 1932, I met the editor of the Melody Maker, who was Percy Brooks at the time.

ctx.x: Good evening and welcome once again to KBS Radio press conference, which for the next few weeks will be without the familiar voice of Chairman Michael Sumner. Normally in press conference, our personality is connected with the world of politics, government, science, commerce and industry. Tonight is the first time we have had anybody from the world of entertainment. On this occasion, we are delighted to have here in the studio none other than the famous jazz musician Louis Armstrong, affectionately known in…

Satchmo, isn't it? Satchmo, yeah. That's the nickname I picked up in England, you know. In England? Yeah, when I went there in 1932, I met the editor of the Melody Maker, who was Percy Brooks at the time. And at that time, my nickname was Satchel Mouth. See, like the valise, you know what I mean? And now, I don't know, when the train pulled up and Percy Brooks come up, he said, hello, Satchmo, you know. So I said, what'd you say, Daddy? You know, that's what we agreed with. And then I asked my trombone player,…
Now, I read somewhere, Mr. Armstrong, that Jack Teagarden once described you as just a little guy with a big mouth, but man, can he blow that horn?
